# delaytensor

> Two attempts to compute with delay lines, simulated and benched. Delay Tensor treats a bundle of coupled transmission lines as a fixed reservoir in front of a linear readout; DLNN trains ternary {-1, 0, +1} weights into the taps of an LC delay line, so the board's pick-and-place file is the model. Everything is simulated, emulated (Verilog RTL) or designed; nothing has been fabricated or measured.

Key results (exact conditions in the linked docs): temporal XOR 0.724 raw vs 0.995 reservoir, and the win comes from the per-slot tanh, not the coupling; six-way classification and MNIST tie within seed spread; the recurrence matches ngspice to 5.27e-16; DLNN scores 0.878 on the simulated board line, 0.17 on the board as designed until a gain bug is fixed, with a 0.6-point spread over 1,000 simulated boards.
